name: Pruritus (hepatobiliary context)
description: Pruritus in a hepatobiliary context is generalised itching caused by accumulation of bile salts, bilirubin, or other pruritogenic substances in the skin due to impaired biliary excretion (cholestasis). It is a cardinal symptom of cholestatic liver disease, including primary biliary cholangitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, and drug-induced cholestasis. Hepatobiliary pruritus is characteristically worse at night, may be most prominent on palms and soles, and is not associated with a primary skin rash. It must be distinguished from dermatological causes of itch by the absence of primary skin lesions and by abnormal liver biochemistry.
